result.title: RASSG: Repair-Aware Semantic Survival Gating for Streaming Tool Execution
result.summary: Streaming speech assistants can launch tools before users finish speaking, overlapping execution with incoming speech to reduce user waiting time. However, subsequent self-corrections can invalidate apparently stable arguments, causing stale execution whose irreversible effects persist even after the final call is corrected. We propose Repair-Aware Semantic Survival Gating (RASSG) to jointly control tool launch and cancellation during streaming speech. RASSG launches a tool when three consecutive speech recognition results arrive with identical nonempty arguments, then combines calibrated argument invalidity risk with execution costs to decide cancellation at the last feasible opportunity before effects become irreversible. Evaluation on ReCAST, FDB-v3, and Audio2Tool uses a controlled execution clock with fixed tool runtimes and cancellation parameters. On ReCAST's prospective-repair subset, RASSG reduces the stale execution rate from LocalAgreement-2's 50.00% to 3.15%, with a mean delay of 3.676s across successful trajectories. The stale reduction also holds against every early-execution baseline on both public speech datasets. Ablations with identical initial launches support active cancellation, showing the value of controlling ongoing calls before their effects become irreversible. Code and data are available at https://github.com/daijinhu/RASSG.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究流式语音助手中工具提前启动的执行风险：用户随后的自我纠正会使看似稳定的参数失效，导致过期执行且效果不可逆。作者提出 RASSG，以连续三次识别结果参数一致作为启动条件，并在效果不可逆前结合校准的参数失效风险与执行成本决定是否取消，在 ReCAST 等数据集上用受控执行时钟评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「证据稳定才提交、在不可逆前取消」的联合控制，可能与 LVR 中 STOP 决策及动态计算、证据获取的收益—成本权衡形成类比，可供核查停止准则与不可逆承诺的建模；但领域相距较远，迁移需较多工作。
